intro: Lesson 56: Constructing triangles: two sides and the included angle (SAS). To understand how to construct a triangle accurately from two sides and the angle between them

model.title: Construct triangle ABC with AB = 7 cm, angle A = 40° and AC = 5 cm.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Draw AB = 7 cm with a ruler

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: At A, measure 40° and draw a long faint line

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: Measure 5 cm along it from A and mark C

questions.q: Construct triangle XYZ with XY = 6 cm, angle X = 70° and XZ = 6 cm. Measure YZ and angles Y and Z.
questions.a: YZ ≈ 6.9 cm; angles Y and Z are both 55°
questions.model: Draw XY = 6 cm, measure 70° at X, mark 6 cm along the arm, join to Y. XY = XZ, so the triangle is isosceles: (180 - 70) ÷ 2 = 55° each.

questions.q: Construct triangle DEF with DE = 5 cm, angle E = 90° and EF = 12 cm. Measure DF.
Construct each triangle and measure the third side: (a) AB = 8 cm, angle A = 60°, AC = 8 cm (b) PQ = 9 cm, angle P = 35°, PR = 6 cm (c) KL = 7.5 cm, angle K = 110°, KM = 4 cm
questions.a: (a) 8 cm (b) QR ≈ 5.3 cm (c) LM ≈ 9.6 cm (accept ± 2 mm)
questions.model: (a) Two 8 cm sides with 60° between them: the other angles are (180 - 60) ÷ 2 = 60° too. The triangle is equilateral, so the third side is also 8 cm.

questions.q: Construct a rhombus with sides of 5 cm and one angle of 50°. Measure the shorter diagonal.
AB = 7 cm, angle A = 40° and BC = 5 cm. Construct both possible triangles. Why are there two?
questions.a: An arc of 5 cm from B cuts the 40° line at A in two places, so C has two positions: the angle is not between the given sides.

questions.q: Which set of facts fixes exactly one triangle?
questions.a: B) two sides and the angle between them
options: two sides and the angle between them

questions.q: How accurate must a constructed length be?
Big question: if I give you two sides and one angle, is there only one triangle?
questions.a: Yes, if the angle is between the two sides (SAS); otherwise there may be two.
